messages.author: 1ffc6ad02dde819f
messages.subject: gl.spatial.autoCorr function
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I was wondering if there is a way I can run spatial autocorrelation using the new function gl.spatial.autoCorr to generate a combined graph for all my populations (similar to how it's done in genalex) instead of having graphs for each population. Should I treat them as a single population? Not sure if it is the way to go and how to do this, though... 

Any help would be greatly appreciated. 

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.spatial.autoCorr function
parts:
Hi Lukiel,
you can achieve this setting to TRUE the argument plot.pops.together when you call the spatial autocorrelation function.

Cheers,
carlo

messages.author: 86913d3f72f6633b
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.spatial.autoCorr function
parts:
Hi Lukiel,
if you would like to have the start points rather than the end points, since the plot is a ggplot object, this can be easily done by modifying the labels on the x-axis. Retrieve the RDS with the ggplot from the temp folder like so (note you can only do this if you select save2tmp=TRUE):
gl.list.reports() # this lists the object saved so you can identify the object number, say your plot is number 2
p<-gl.print.reports(2) # this stores the object number 2 (the ggplot) into 'p'
scale_x_continuous(labels = seq(0,1000, 250)) # This replace the labels with the start points

Cheers,
carlo

messages.author: 86913d3f72f6633b
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.spatial.autoCorr function
parts:
Hi Lukiel,
Yes, this is correct, you are just replacing the labels, but keep in mind that the lower limit is always included in the analysis - that is [min-max), so in the first distance class where 0 is the lower limit, 0 is included. As a reference, in all the other distance classes the same approach is used, except the last one in which the end point is also included - i.e. [min-max].

Cheers,
carlo
